beats.label: S1 · The pact
beats.text: At Miranda's birthday party, four single friends in their late thirties vow to stop chasing 'perfect' men and start having sex like men do — without feelings.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's premise and the frame every relationship beat is measured against.

beats.label: S1 · Enter Mr. Big
beats.text: Carrie keeps colliding with tycoon Mr. Big around town. He is charming, elusive, and immediately the exception to the no-feelings rule she just made.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the central relationship that drives every Carrie beat that follows.

beats.label: S1 · Drink thing to dating
beats.text: A first proper date turns into something recurring, but Carrie learns Big is still seeing other women and pushes for a real answer about what they are.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shifts Carrie and Big from flirtation to a defined thing she can be hurt by.

beats.label: S1 · The ex-wife
beats.text: Carrie discovers Big was married once and once had a threesome. The past he has not mentioned starts to feel like the shape of what he will not give her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First concrete evidence Big is guarded about his real life with her.

beats.label: S1 · Never again
beats.text: Big tells Carrie he never wants to get married again. She keeps dating him anyway, filing it away as something she can work around.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the fundamental incompatibility that Carrie spends the rest of the series pretending isn't there.

beats.label: S1 · Miranda and Skipper
beats.text: Miranda drifts in and out of nice-guy Skipper, sleeping with him, getting jealous when he moves on, unable to decide if 'nice' is enough for her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Miranda's pattern of sabotaging the exact men who treat her well.

beats.label: S1 · 'A friend'
beats.text: Big introduces Carrie to his mother as 'a friend'. She sees the whole relationship is one-sided, ends it, and spends Christmas single.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the state the reader walks into next season — Carrie and Big broken up over his refusal to acknowledge her.

cliffhanger.text: Carrie has walked away from Big after he refused to acknowledge her as more than 'a friend' to his mother. The four women's experiment in loveless sex has, for Carrie at least, quietly collapsed into wanting the thing she said she didn't.
questions: Will Big come back once he realises what he lost, or was 'a friend' the truth?
Can Miranda ever accept a man as decent as Skipper, or will she keep pushing him away?
Will Charlotte's search for a husband survive the city's supply of men?

characters.name: Carrie Bradshaw
characters.line: Sex columnist and narrator; just ended things with Mr. Big after he wouldn't call her his girlfriend to his own mother.

characters.name: Mr. Big
characters.line: Wealthy, older, charming tycoon Carrie has been seeing; divorced, allergic to commitment, and now her ex.

characters.name: Miranda Hobbes
characters.line: Skeptical corporate lawyer, sharpest of the four; sleeping with nice-guy Skipper on and off and hating that she cares.

characters.name: Charlotte York
characters.line: Uptown gallerist and the group's romantic; still single, still convinced marriage is coming, quietly panicking that it isn't.

characters.name: Samantha Jones
characters.line: PR powerhouse and unapologetic hedonist; the only one still fully committed to the sex-like-men pact.

characters.name: Skipper Johnston
characters.line: Sweet, earnest tech guy set up with Miranda; keeps getting picked up and dropped by her.

characters.name: Stanford Blatch
characters.line: Carrie's gay best friend and confidant; talent manager navigating his own family's expectations of marriage.
